title: Cartesian associative algebras and Segal simplicial objects
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations and edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], the simplex category and inert maps of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and the cartesian monoidal envelope of [lem-coef-cartesian-operadic-envelope]. Let $\mathcal C$ be an infinity category with finite products, including a terminal object for the empty product. Write $\mathsf{Fin}_*$ for finite pointed sets and $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$. Choose the product-diagram model $\mathcal C^\times\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and its coherent product-evaluation functor $\pi:\mathcal C^\times\to\mathcal C$ from [lem-coef-cartesian-envelope-product-diagram-recognition]: a tuple has image its product, and an arrow has image the tuple of its block maps precomposed with the input projections.

Let $\mathsf{Ass}$ be the ordinary symmetric operad with one color whose operations on a finite labeled input set are its linear orders; substitution concatenates the ordered input lists, the nullary operation is the empty list and the unary identity is the singleton list. Its category of operators $\mathsf{Ass}^\otimes$ has objects $\langle n\rangle$, and a morphism is a pointed map together with a linear order on each non-basepoint fiber; composition substitutes these lists and discards inputs sent to the basepoint. Write $u:\mathsf{Ass}^\otimes\to\mathsf{Fin}_*$ for the forgetful functor. Put $\mathcal C^\times_{\mathsf{Ass}}=\mathcal C^\times\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}N(\mathsf{Ass}^\otimes)$. Let $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathsf{Ass}}(\mathcal C^\times)$ denote the full infinity category of sections of this pullback carrying inert arrows to cocartesian arrows, with coherent transformations over the identity of the base; inert means that each non-basepoint output has exactly one preimage.

Define $\operatorname{Cut}:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Ass}^\otimes$ by $\operatorname{Cut}([n])=\langle n\rangle$. For $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ with opposite $a:[m]\to[n]$, it sends $j$ to $i$ if $a(i-1)<j\leq a(i)$ and to $*$ otherwise, ordering each fiber by its input indices. Let $\mathcal C^\times_{\mathrm{pl}}$ be the pullback along $N(\operatorname{Cut})$, and let $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ be its infinity category of inert-preserving sections, in the nonsymmetric convention of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Let $\operatorname{Mon}_\Delta(\mathcal C)$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}),\mathcal C)$ on diagrams $F$ whose inert edge maps exhibit $F([n])\simeq F([1])^n$ as a product cone for every $n\geq0$.

Restriction along $N(\operatorname{Cut})$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathsf{Ass}}(\mathcal C^\times)\simeq\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathrm{pl}}$. Composition with the specified $\pi$ after restriction induces an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathsf{Ass}}(\mathcal C^\times)\simeq\operatorname{Mon}_\Delta(\mathcal C).$$
These equivalences preserve the underlying-object functor to $\mathcal C$. They identify the $r$-ary operation $x^r\to x$ for the standard input order with the transport along the endpoint-preserving arrow $[r]\to[1]$, under the Segal product cone; arity zero gives the unit. They identify the entire infinity categories, including mapping spaces and all higher families. For an algebra morphism with underlying map $f:x\to y$, the corresponding transformation has degree-$n$ component $f^n$ under the product-cone identifications. The equivalences are natural in finite-product-preserving functors. No other limits or any colimits are required.
